name: Change requests
description: Provides change requests (proposed edits) for nodes, stored field-by-field in a separate 'patch' entity independent of the node revision history.
project_description: Change Requests lets multiple users collaborate on Drupal node content without edit-wars, in a workflow inspired by the git "pull request". Authorized users edit a node through the normal node form, but their changes are not written to the node; instead they are captured field-by-field as programmatic change statements ("patch") in a separate 'patch' content entity, completely independent of the node's revision history. A patch stores diffs such as "in field_body replace 'Peter and Mary' with 'Peter or Mary'" and "in field_tags remove target_id 23 and add 45". Patches are shown as a highlighted diff view, reviewed by the community or editors, and later applied to the node. Applying a change request produces a new node revision whose log message records the patch author, date, link and title, so all changes remain transparent (e.g. via the Diff module). Because content may change between creation and acceptance, applying uses a merge interface: the diff on the left and the auto-merged result as editable widgets on the right, so merge conflicts can be resolved before saving. Almost all Drupal core field types are supported through a FieldPatchPlugin plugin type; custom field types can add support via the documented plugin interface. Text diffs use Google's diff-match-patch library ported to PHP by yetanotherape. Depends on the Changed Field API (changed_fields) module.
